# BCH expansion and exponentials of operators

## Introduction

Coupled-cluster calculations use exponentials of operators. We will treat the
operators as finite square matrices. For a square matrix $T$, define the matrix
exponential by the power series

$$
\exp(T) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{T^n}{n!}.
$$ {#eq-matrix-exponential}

The zeroth power is the identity matrix, $T^0=I$.

## Exercises

:::{#exr-matrix-exponential}

Consider the matrix exponential in @eq-matrix-exponential.

a. Write the first five terms of the power series.

b. Explain why $T$ must be square for every term in the series to be defined.

c. Let

   $$
   T =
   \begin{bmatrix}
   0 & 1 \\
   -1 & 0
   \end{bmatrix}.
   $$

   Compute $T^2$, $T^3$, and $T^4$. Use the results to evaluate the degree-four
   approximation to $\exp(T)$.

:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="tutor"}

## Solutions

### Solution to @exr-matrix-exponential

a. Substituting $n=0,1,2,3,4$ in @eq-matrix-exponential gives

   $$
   \exp(T)
   = I + T + \frac{1}{2}T^2 + \frac{1}{6}T^3
   + \frac{1}{24}T^4 + \cdots.
   $$

b. The product $T^2=TT$ requires the number of columns of the first factor to
   equal the number of rows of the second. Repeated powers $T^n$ therefore keep
   the same dimensions only when $T$ is square. The identity $I=T^0$ must have
   those dimensions as well.

c. Direct multiplication gives

   $$
   T^2=-I, \qquad T^3=-T, \qquad T^4=I.
   $$

   The degree-four approximation is

   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   I + T + \frac{1}{2}T^2 + \frac{1}{6}T^3 + \frac{1}{24}T^4
   &= I + T - \frac{1}{2}I - \frac{1}{6}T + \frac{1}{24}I \\
   &= \frac{13}{24}I + \frac{5}{6}T \\
   &=
   \begin{bmatrix}
   13/24 & 5/6 \\
   -5/6 & 13/24
   \end{bmatrix}.
   \end{aligned}
   $$

:::
